He played [[college football]] for the [[Wisconsin Badgers football|Wisconsin Badgers]]. He was selected by the [[Minnesota Vikings]] in the first round of the [[2001 NFL draft]] with the 27th overall pick. A [[Pro Bowl]] selection with the Vikings in [[2003 Pro Bowl|2002]], Bennett was also a member of the [[New Orleans Saints]], [[Kansas City Chiefs]], [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]], [[San Diego Chargers]], and [[Oakland Raiders]].

'''Michael Paul Bishop''' (born May 15, 1976) is an American former professional [[gridiron football|football]] player who was a [[quarterback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL), [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL), [[Arena Football League (1987–2008)|Arena Football League]] (AFL), and [[NFL Europe]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Kansas State Wildcats football|Kansas State Wildcats]], earning consensus [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honors in 1998. He was selected by the [[New England Patriots]] in the seventh round of the [[1999 NFL draft]].

Bishop was a member of the CFL's [[Toronto Argonauts]] from 2002 to 2008. He also previously played with the NFL's [[New England Patriots]] during the [[2000 NFL season|2000]] season.

Bishop was one of the best college quarterbacks in the country at Kansas State, beating out [[UCLA Bruins football|UCLA's]] [[Cade McNown]] for the [[1998 NCAA Division I-A football season|1998]] [[Davey O'Brien Award]]. Bishop was elected to the [[College Football Hall of Fame]] in 2023.<ref name="i282">{{cite web | last=Reinhardt | first=Landon | title=K-State’s Michael Bishop elected to College Football Hall of Fame | website=KSNT 27 News | date=2023-01-09 | url=https://www.ksnt.com/sports/kansas-state-wildcats/k-states-michael-bishop-elected-to-college-football-hall-of-fame/ | access-date=2024-10-17}}</ref>

'''Michael Dean Perry''' (born August 27, 1965) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive lineman]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He is the younger brother of [[William Perry (American football)|William Perry]]. His parents are Inez S. Perry and Hollie Perry Sr. of Aiken, South Carolina.  He learned to play football from his older brothers. He attended South Aiken High School where he anchored the offensive and defensive line. He played [[college football]] for the [[Clemson Tigers football|Clemson Tigers]] and set the school record of 28 [[Quarterback sack|sacks]] (tied by [[defensive end]] [[Gaines Adams]] in 2006 and then broken by [[Vic Beasley]] in 2014).<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.sportsline.com/nfl/players/draft/405275 |title=Gaines Adams player profile at CBS Sportsline |access-date=2007-04-30}}</ref><ref>[http://www.foxsports.com/south/story/beasley-tops-perry-adams-to-become-clemson-all-time-sack-king-101114 Beasley tops Perry, Adams to become Clemson all-time sack king]</ref> He was later drafted by the [[Cleveland Browns]] in the second round of the [[1988 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1988 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1988/draft.htm |access-date=2023-09-24 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He played in the [[Pro Bowl]] six times and played for the Browns, the [[Denver Broncos]], and the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] over his 10-year career.

Michael Dean Perry was one of the more televised players in Cleveland during his stay with the Browns. He also at one time had a [[McDonald's]] sandwich named in his honor. The sandwich was named the "MDP". The "MDP" was available only in the Metro Cleveland area. The sandwich at the time was larger than any offering made by McDonald's. It consisted of the same ingredients as a double cheeseburger with the addition of a patty and bacon.<ref>{{cite web |title=McDonald's MDP Commercial | website=[[YouTube]] | date=February 24, 2015 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ibmaP9dMTho  |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211221/ibmaP9dMTho |archive-date=2021-12-21 |url-status=live|access-date=22 October 2018}}{{cbignore}}</ref>
